text.paragraph_1: the façade is a “desktop”; the windows are application icons. browser tabs and system notifications appear in the storefront we look at every day. here architecture ceases to be merely stone and glass: it becomes the user interface of reality. an ordinary rectangular opening turns into a dialogue box with a “close tab” function. people have grown used to looking at the street through a monitor and at the monitor through a window, long forgetting where the interface ends and reality begins.
text.paragraph_2: the city is an operating system in which each of us is both a user and a notification.
text.paragraph_3: in this project, i combine window grilles with the windows of interface space. addressing digital habit, the window grille becomes a visual analogue of the screen grid through which people are accustomed to perceiving reality. i merge these structures to emphasise that the boundaries between the physical and the virtual have dissolved, and that we look at the world through the prism of algorithms embedded within us.
